statement: A discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) system with impulse response h[n] is bounded-input, bounded-output (BIBO) stable if its impulse response is absolutely summable (\|h\|_1 = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[n]| \in \mathbb{R}$), in which case every bounded input x[n] with $\|x\|_\infty < \infty$ produces a bounded output y[n] satisfying $|y[n]| \leq \|x\|_\infty \|h\|_1 < \infty$.

symbols.meaning: impulse response of the discrete-time LTI system
L-infinity norm (maximum absolute value) of the input signal
L-1 norm (absolute sum) of the impulse response

steps.text: For a discrete-time LTI system with impulse response $h[n]$ and input $x[n]$, express the output $y[n]$ via the definition of convolution: $y[n] = h[n] * x[n] = \sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} h[n-k] x[k]$.
Take the absolute value of the output and apply the triangle inequality to the summation: $|y[n]| = \left|\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} h[n-k] x[k]\right| \leq \sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[n-k]| |x[k]|$.

Bound $|x[k]|$ by its supremum norm $\|x\|_\infty = \sup_n |x[n]|$ and factor it out of the summation: $\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[n-k]| |x[k]| \leq \sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[n-k]| \|x\|_\infty = \|x\|_\infty \sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[n-k]| = \|x\|_\infty \sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[k]|$.

Apply the condition that $h[n]$ is absolutely summable, so $\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[k]| = \|h\|_1 \in \mathbb{R}$, yielding $|y[n]| \leq \|x\|_\infty \sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[k]| = \|x\|_\infty \|h\|_1$.

Conclude that if $h[n]$ is absolutely summable ($\|h\|_1 \in \mathbb{R}$) and the input is bounded ($|x[n]|$ is bounded, so $\|x\|_\infty \in \mathbb{R}$), then the output is bounded ($|y[n]| \leq \|x\|_\infty \|h\|_1 \in \mathbb{R}$), establishing BIBO stability.

assumptions.assumption: The system is a discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) system.
assumptions.breaks_when: The system is nonlinear or time-varying, so the relationship between input and output cannot be expressed as convolution with an impulse response.

assumptions.assumption: The impulse response h[n] is absolutely summable: $\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} |h[n]| = \|h\|_1 \in \mathbb{R}$.
assumptions.breaks_when: The sum of absolute values of the impulse response diverges ($\|h\|_1 = \infty$).

assumptions.assumption: The input signal x[n] is bounded: $\|x\|_\infty < \infty$.

failure_modes.signature: The output y[n] diverges or grows without bound despite a bounded input x[n].
failure_modes.cause: The impulse response h[n] is not absolutely summable (\|h\|_1 \notin \mathbb{R}).

failure_modes.mode: Unbounded input leading to unbounded output
failure_modes.signature: Output magnitude |y[n]| is not guaranteed to remain finite.
failure_modes.cause: The input signal x[n] is unbounded (\|x\|_\infty \notin \mathbb{R}).
